381851.title: The simply connected level-set conjecture for checkerboard switching
381851.statement_literal:
Let $R\in\mathbb{N}^p$, $C\in\mathbb{N}^q$, and let $\mathbf{M}\in\mathcal{M}_{p,q}(\{-1,0,1\})$. For each integer $i$, let $\mathcal{P}_i(\mathbf{M})$ denote the set of cells at level $i$ associated with $\mathbf{M}$, and let $\mathbf{C}_{i,i+1,k,k+1}$ denote the corresponding elementary $2\times2$ checkerboard move. Write $\mathbf{A}\rightarrow\mathbf{A}'$ for the switching relation on matrices in $\mathcal{M}(R,C)$. **The simply connected level-set conjecture.** We have $\mathbf{A}\rightarrow\mathbf{A}'$ for all $\mathbf{A},\mathbf{A}'\in\mathcal{M}(R,C)$ such that $\mathbf{A}'-\mathbf{A}=\mathbf{M}$ if and only if both of the following conditions hold: (i) there exists $\mathbf{T}\in\mathcal{M}_{p-1,q-1}(\mathbb{N})$ such that

$$
\mathbf{M}=\sum_{i,k}t_{ik}\mathbf{C}_{i,i+1,k,k+1};
$$

(ii) for every $i$, each connected component of $\mathcal{P}_i(\mathbf{M})$ is simply connected. The conjecture removes condition (iii) from the preceding sufficient theorem and predicts that failure of simple connectivity is exactly the obstruction to universal switchability.
381851.review_depth: full source TeX (arXiv:2212.07706 v1, only version) Sections 2-3 read: definitions, Prop. NC, Lemma m_ij, Lemma no-diag-touching, Theorem SC (conditions i-iii), Conjecture; web/citing search (no later work found)
381851.disposition: Ellison-Jouve-Stone conjecture (switching checkerboards). The printed quantifier fixes (R,C): the left side is vacuous when no pair has difference M, and the fixed-(R,C) "only if" already fails at R=C=(1,1,1,1) with the source's own Example 2 matrix M (the unique pair, permutation matrices, is reachable although P_1(M) is a ring): formulation defects, zero credit. Substantive "if" direction ((i)+(ii) => A->A', i.e. condition (iii) of Theorem SC unnecessary) tested exhaustively: all 3x3 (512), 4x4 (65,536) and 4x5 (1,048,576; 16 chunks) binary matrices, reachability closure of every class G(R,C); 12,818,863 ordered dominance-comparable pairs (cond (i) <=> 2D prefix-sum dominance); only 112 comparable pairs are unreachable and every one fails (ii). No counterexample. 5x5 (33.5M matrices) exceeds the lane caps; a targeted search over (iii)-violating T was designed but not run.

381931.title: The chirotopal tropical Grassmannian conjecture for rank three
381931.statement_literal:
Fix a realizable chirotope $\chi\in\{-1,1\}^{\binom{n}{3}}$. Let $\operatorname{Dr}^\chi_{3,n}$ be the chirotopal Dressian, consisting of the $\chi$-tropical Plücker vectors, and let $\operatorname{Trop}^\chi G(3,n)$ be the realizable $\chi$-tropical Grassmannian. Work modulo the lineality space consisting of vectors with coordinates

$$
\pi_J=\sum_{j\in J}x_j
$$

for $x\in\mathbb R^n$. **Chirotopal tropical Grassmannian conjecture.** Each $\operatorname{Dr}^\chi_{3,n}$ is a pure $(3-1)(n-3-1)$-dimensional polyhedral fan, and

$$
\operatorname{Trop}^\chi G(3,n)=\operatorname{Dr}^\chi_{3,n}.
$$

Moreover, for any fixed maximal cone in $\operatorname{Trop}G(3,n)$, either the cone is contained in no chirotopal tropical Grassmannian, or it is contained in exactly $2^{(3-1)(n-3-1)}$ of them. The conjecture generalizes the known characterization of the positive tropical Grassmannian by the three-term tropical Plücker relations; it asserts realizability for all rank-three realizable chirotopes and includes the stated purity and counting properties.
381931.review_depth: abstract v1-v4 (SIGMA 20 (2024) 016); citing work Antolini-Early arXiv:2411.07293 abstract read
381931.disposition: Cachazo-Early-Zhang chirotopal tropical Grassmannian conjecture (rank 3). Antolini-Early (Le Matematiche 2025) prove Trop^chi G(3,n)=Dr^chi(3,n) for n=6,7,8 and show failure for (4,8); n>=9 open. Next case needs polyhedral fan computations over all rank-3 realizable chirotopes on 9 elements (no polymake/solver in this lane). Parked.

381982.title: Capparelli–Meurman–Primc–Primc odd-modulus conjecture
381982.statement_literal:
Let $k_0,\ldots,k_n$ be non-negative integers, let $E_1$ be the set of parts, and let $\mathcal{Q}^{k_0,\ldots,k_n}_{\mathds{1}}$ be the partitions into parts in $E_1$ whose frequencies, augmented by fictitious occurrences with $f_{(-1)_{2n-1-2i}}=k_i$ for $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and $f_{(0)_0}=k_n$, satisfy

$$
f_{e_0}+\cdots+f_{e_{2n-1}}\leq k_0+\cdots+k_n
$$

for every path $(e_0,\ldots,e_{2n-1})$ of $E_{-1}$. Write $k=k_0+\cdots+k_n$. **CMPP odd conjecture.** One has

$$
\sum_{\pi\in\mathcal{Q}^{k_0,\ldots,k_n}_{\mathds{1}}}q^{|\pi|}=\frac{\prod_{a\in \{2n+2k+1\}^n;b\in \Delta(k_1+1,\ldots,k_n+1);\ j=a,b,2n+2k+1-b}(q^j;q^{2n+2k+1})_\infty}{(q;q)_\infty^n}.
$$

This is the odd-modulus analogue attributed in the paper to Capparelli, Meurman, Primc and Primc; the case $n=1$ recovers the Andrews–Gordon identities. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
381982.review_depth: source abstract (Dousse-Konan arXiv:2212.12728 v1); CMPP arXiv:2106.06262 and Kanade-Russell-Tsuchioka-Warnaar arXiv:2404.03851 (Selecta 2026) abstracts
381982.disposition: Odd-modulus CMPP partition identity for all (k_0..k_n). Source proves the level-1 case; KRTW relate the remaining CMPP families to A_{2n}^{(2)}, D_{n+1}^{(2)} specialisations without (per abstract) a full proof. An infinite product identity; coefficient checks cannot prove it and the authors/KRTW verified it numerically. No finite certificate route; parked (abstract-level status, not body-verified).

349920.title: Independence-of-$\ell$ conjecture for the spectral Bernstein center map
349920.statement_literal:
Let $G$ be a reductive group over the local field $E$, let $W_E$ be its Weil group, and let $\mathcal Z^{\mathrm{spec}}(G,\mathbb Q)$ be the natural rational form of the spectral Bernstein center. For every prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\mathbb Q_\ell(\sqrt q)$ for the corresponding coefficient field. **Independence-of-$\ell$ conjecture.** There is a necessarily unique map

$$
\mathcal Z^{\mathrm{spec}}(G,\mathbb Q(\sqrt q))\to\mathcal Z(G(E),\mathbb Q(\sqrt q))
$$

whose base change to every $\mathbb Q_\ell$ with $\ell\neq p$ is the composite

$$
\mathcal Z^{\mathrm{spec}}(G,\mathbb Q_\ell(\sqrt q))\to\mathcal Z^{\mathrm{geom}}(G,\mathbb Q_\ell(\sqrt q))\to\mathcal Z(G(E),\mathbb Q_\ell(\sqrt q)).
$$

This would make the constructed $L$-parameters independent of $\ell$ in the relevant sense; related conjectures concern the stable Bernstein center and the image of this map.
349920.disposition: Independence-of-l for the spectral Bernstein centre map (Fargues-Scholze). Deep arithmetic geometry; no finite route. Disposed quickly per brief.

350007.title: Aboulker et al.'s conjecture on heroic triples of oriented star forests
350007.statement_literal: An **oriented graph** is a digraph with no digons, and its dichromatic number $\vec{\chi}(D)$ is the least number of acyclic sets partitioning its vertex set. A digraph is a **heroic set** obstruction when the class of digraphs excluding every member of the set as an induced subdigraph has bounded dichromatic number; a **hero** is a tournament with this property when it is the sole nontrivial forbidden tournament. **Aboulker et al.'s conjecture.** For every orientation of a star forest $F$ and every hero $H$, the oriented graphs excluding $F$ and $H$ as induced subdigraphs have bounded dichromatic number. This is the third type in the proposed classification of heroic sets of size three; the source notes that it is known for transitive $H$ and when $F$ has at most two vertices, but remains open in general.
350007.disposition: Aboulker et al. heroic-triple conjecture (oriented star forests + hero). Infinite chi-boundedness statement; refutation needs an infinite family, proof is structural. Near the parked 371680 acyclic-heroes family. Parked; later literature not body-checked.

350024.title: Spiro's descent–cyclic excedance conjecture for ballot and odd-order permutations
350024.statement_literal:
Let $\mathcal{B}_n$ be the set of ballot permutations of $[n]$, and let $\mathcal{O}_n$ be the set of permutations of $[n]$ whose cycles all have odd length. For a permutation $\pi$, write $\mathsf{des}(\pi)$ for its descent number. If $C$ ranges over the cycles of $\pi$, let $\mathsf{casc}(C)$ and $\mathsf{cdes}(C)$ denote its cyclic ascent and cyclic descent numbers, and define

$$
\widetilde\mathsf{exc}(\pi)=\sum_C\min(\mathsf{casc}(C),\mathsf{cdes}(C)).
$$

**Spiro's conjecture.** For every $n\geq1$,

$$
\sum_{\pi\in\mathcal{B}_n}t^{\mathsf{des}(\pi)}=\sum_{\pi\in\mathcal{O}_n}t^{\widetilde\mathsf{exc}(\pi)}.
$$

This conjecture refines the equality $|\mathcal{B}_n|=|\mathcal{O}_n|$ by asserting equality of the corresponding descent and modified excedance polynomials. Several important special cases were known when Spiro posed it; the supplied text gives no resolution of the full conjecture.
350024.review_depth: source TeX Section 1 read (Lin-Wang-Zhao arXiv:2103.04599): Conjecture 1.1 = Spiro Conjecture 1.2; text states Wang-Zhao proved it
350024.disposition: Spiro descent / cyclic-excedance equidistribution. Proved by Wang-Zhao (arXiv:2009.05973, generating functions) and bijectively by the source itself. Same family as 345225 (excluded known in r168).

350106.title: The disk minimisation conjecture for the lowest positive Dirac eigenvalue
350106.statement_literal:
Let $m\geq 0$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be an open connected set with locally Lipschitz boundary, and let $\lambda_1(\Omega)$ denote the lowest positive eigenvalue of the Dirac operator with infinite-mass boundary conditions. For a disk $\Omega^*$, impose either equality of area or equality of perimeter with $\Omega$. **Disk minimisation conjecture.** For every $m\geq 0$,

$$
\lambda_1(\Omega)\geq\lambda_1(\Omega^*)
$$

when $\Omega^*$ has the same area as $\Omega$, and

$$
\lambda_1(\Omega)\geq\lambda_1(\Omega^*)
$$

when $\Omega^*$ has the same perimeter as $\Omega$. This is the relativistic analogue of the Faber–Krahn inequality. The area-constrained massless case was previously stated as a conjecture, and the general problem remains open; it has been identified as a hot open problem in spectral geometry.
350106.disposition: Faber-Krahn analogue for the infinite-mass Dirac operator; analytic spectral geometry (the source itself only treats rectangles, with a gap in v1). Parked.

350481.title: Green–Liebeck code conjecture for conjugacy classes in symmetric groups
350481.statement_literal: Let $n>2k$ and let $j$ satisfy $2^j\leq k<2^{j+1}$. Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, let $X=x^{S_n}$ be the conjugacy class of $x$ in $S_n$, and let $Y_k$ denote the code subset from the Green–Liebeck setting. For subsets $X,Y$ of a finite group, write $\lambda G=XY$ when every element of $G$ has exactly $\lambda$ representations as a product $xy$ with $(x,y)\in X\times Y$; in this case $X$ and $Y$ divide $G$. **Green–Liebeck code conjecture.** The factorization $\lambda S_n=XY_k$ holds if and only if the cycle-type of $x$ has exactly one cycle of length $2^i$ for every $0\leq i\leq j$, and all other cycles have length at least $k+1$. This conjecture concerns perfect and multiple codes in symmetric groups and was proposed by Holly M. Green and Martin W. Liebeck; the supplied paper studies it through combinatorial identities, but provides no resolution.
350481.review_depth: Pan arXiv:2104.10346 full TeX; Fang-Li arXiv:2502.10744 abstract v1-v2
350481.disposition: Green-Liebeck Conjecture 2.3 (Y_k = S_k x S_{n-k}). Proved by Fang and Li, arXiv:2502.10744 (Feb 2025, v2 Dec 2025). Lane note: via permutation characters (chi^{(n-i,i)} = pi_i - pi_{i-1}) the condition is that x fixes exactly one i-subset for each i<=k, which a two-line induction reduces to the binary cycle-type condition; in any case known.

350580.title: The growable-realizations conjecture for admissible multisets
350580.statement_literal:
Let $U$ be a fixed set of positive integers. A multiset $L$ is **admissible** when it satisfies the necessary divisibility conditions in the Buratti-Horak-Rosa conjecture, and a **growable realization** is a realization with the growth property developed in the paper.

**Growable-realizations conjecture.** For any fixed set $U$, there is a finite set of growable realizations with underlying set $U$ that implies the existence of realizations for all but finitely many admissible multisets $L$ having underlying set $U$.

If true, this would show that the growable-realization method is universally successful for each fixed underlying set, reducing the Buratti-Horak-Rosa conjecture to finitely many exceptional multisets. The paper proves several small underlying-set cases and partial results, but the stated general claim remains open.
350580.disposition: Growable-realizations conjecture: for each U a finite set of growable realizations covers all but finitely many admissible L. A meta-statement about the method for every U; neither finitely refutable nor provable by bounded computation. Parked.

350969.title: The geometric model conjecture for dimer tree algebras
350969.statement_literal:
Let $B$ be a dimer tree algebra, let $\mathcal{S}$ be its checkerboard polygon with $2N$ vertices, and let $\gamma$ be a 2-diagonal. For the projective modules $P_0(\gamma)$ and $P_1(\gamma)$ determined by the degree-zero and degree-one radical-line crossings of $\gamma$, let $\Omega$ denote the syzygy functor. **Geometric model conjecture.** For every 2-diagonal $\gamma$ there exists a morphism

$$
f_\gamma\colon P_1(\gamma)\to P_0(\gamma)
$$

such that $\gamma\mapsto\operatorname{coker}f_\gamma$ induces an equivalence

$$
F\colon\operatorname{Diag}(\mathcal{S})\to\underline{\operatorname{CMP}}\,B.
$$

Under this equivalence, $\rho(i)$ corresponds to $\operatorname{rad}P(i)$, clockwise rotation $R$ corresponds to $\Omega$, $R^2$ corresponds to $\tau^{-1}=\Omega^2$, 2-pivots correspond to irreducible morphisms, and meshes correspond to Auslander–Reiten triangles. The conjecture is the paper's central categorical model for syzygies; no resolution evidence is supplied in the input.
350969.review_depth: abstract v1-v3 (Schiffler-Serhiyenko; v3 5 Aug 2026 adds condition (Q3))
350969.disposition: Geometric model conjecture for syzygies over dimer tree algebras; v3 abstract still proves only the case of chordless cycles of length 3. Deep representation theory; parked.

350973.title: Positivity conjecture for frieze patterns of type $\Lambda_{p_1,\ldots,p_s}$
350973.statement_literal:
Let a frieze pattern be of Type $\Lambda_{p_1,\ldots,p_s}$, and let the realizability test be the criterion given in Proposition. A **frieze pattern of Type $\Lambda_{p_1,\ldots,p_s}$** is understood in the sense of the paper, and a **quotient dissection** is a dissection whose associated frieze pattern is obtained by the quotient construction.

**Positivity conjecture.** The only frieze patterns of Type $\Lambda_{p_1,\ldots,p_s}$ with negative entries are those which fail the realizability test. In particular, all quotient dissections yield frieze patterns with positive entries.

This conjecture proposes that failure of the realizability test exactly accounts for negative entries, extending the positivity result proved under the sufficient condition in Proposition. The examples preceding the conjecture show unrealizable patterns with both positive and negative entries, while the general assertion for all quotient dissections remains open in the supplied text.
350973.review_depth: full source TeX read for all definitions used (Def. 1.1, Section 2, Prop. 4.2, skeletal def., Prop. 4.4, Def. 5.3 + Example 5.4, Theorem 5.4 and proof, cutting, Realization Algorithm, Section 9); citing work Cuntz-Holm-Jorgensen arXiv:2603.18975 TeX grepped; web searches; registry screen
350973.disposition: Banaian-Chen Conjecture 9.5 is false. Explicit quotient dissection (Def. 5.3) of the annulus A_{4,3}: regions (a,b)=(0,1),(2,0),(0,2),(2,0) (triangle + three squares), identify the two outer squares R1,R3 (share v0,v2, no shared arc) exactly as in the source Example 5.4; quiddity (1+sqrt2, sqrt2, 2sqrt2, sqrt2), A=({3,4},{4},{4,4},{4}) passes the Prop. 4.2 test, is skeletal, infinite (proved), and m_{0,11} = 31-22 sqrt2 < 0 (exact). Caveats: the literal first sentence is already contradicted by the source's own example (1+sqrt2,1,2,1+sqrt2) (zero at row 5, negative -(sqrt2-1)); the source Theorem 5.4 proof also fails for ({5},{5},{4,5}). Credit risk HIGH (source-internal literal conflict; short modification of printed Example 5.4; REU preprint). See CANDIDATE-350973.md.

351924.title: The asymmetric Cauchy–Schwarz complexity conjecture
351924.statement_literal:
Let $\Phi=(\phi_1,\dots,\phi_k)$ be a system of linear forms, with $\phi_i\colon\mathbb{F}_p^d\to\mathbb{F}_p$, and let $i_0\in[k]$. Let $s(\Phi,i_0)$ be the asymmetric true complexity of the distinguished form. **Asymmetric Cauchy–Schwarz conjecture.** There should exist $M\geq0$ such that, for every $n\geq1$ and every collection of $1$-bounded functions $f_1,\dots,f_k\colon\mathbb{F}_p^n\to\mathbb{C}$, one has

$$
\left\lvert\Lambda_{\Phi}(f_1,\dots,f_k)\right\rvert\leq\|f_{i_0}\|_{U^{s(\Phi,i_0)+1}}^{2^{-M}}.
$$

The claim also requires that this bound be provable using only repeated applications of Cauchy–Schwarz. The symmetric analogue is handled by the paper's main theorem, whereas natural systems satisfying the asymmetric statement remain open; the conjectured proof method is intended as a test case for strengthening Cauchy–Schwarz arguments.
351924.disposition: Asymmetric true-complexity bound provable by iterated Cauchy-Schwarz; higher-order Fourier analysis, no finite certificate. Parked.

353037.title: Functional relations under symplectic exchange for topological-recursion differentials
353037.statement_literal:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a compact Riemann surface. Let $x$ and $w$ be meromorphic functions on $\mathcal{C}$ such that $\mathrm{d}x$ and $\mathrm{d}w$ have no common zeroes, and let $\mathcal{B}$ be a fundamental bidifferential of the second kind. Denote by $\omega_{g,n}$ the differentials obtained by topological recursion from $(\mathcal{C},x,w,\mathcal{B})$, and by $\omega_{g,n}^{\vee}$ those obtained from $(\mathcal{C},w,x,\mathcal{B})$. Define

$$
\widetilde{\omega}_{0,2}=\widetilde{\omega}_{0,2}^{\vee}=\mathcal{B}.
$$

**Functional-relations conjecture.** For every $2g-2+n\geq 0$, these differentials satisfy the functional relations of Theorem~, after those relations are expressed as relations between meromorphic differentials on $\mathcal{C}$.
This is a proposed general relation between topological recursion and the symplectic exchange $x\mapsto w$. The supplied material does not provide a resolution status or explain the precise functional relations beyond the cited theorem.
353037.disposition: Functional relations for topological recursion under x<->y symplectic exchange. Deep; plausibly addressed by later x-y swap work of Alexandrov-Bychkov-Dunin-Barkowski-Kazarian-Shadrin (unverified lead, not read). No finite route; parked.

345116.title: Duality conjecture for planar scaffold equations
345116.statement_literal:
Let $\{\mathsf{S}_k\}$ be a collection of $m^{\rm th}$ order planar scaffolds whose edge weights belong to $A_0,A_1,\ldots,A_\delta$. Suppose that, for every association scheme with $d\geq\delta$ classes, the scaffold equations

$$
\sum_{k=1}^{n_j}\alpha_{jk}\mathsf{S}_k=\mathbf{0}\qquad(1\leq j\leq n)
$$

together imply

$$
\sum_{k=1}^{n_0}\beta_k\mathsf{S}_k=\mathbf{0}.
$$

**Duality conjecture.** For every association scheme with $d\geq\delta$ classes, the dual scaffold equations

$$
\sum_{k=1}^{n_j}\alpha_{jk}\mathsf{S}_k^\dagger=\mathbf{0}\qquad(1\leq j\leq n)
$$

together imply

$$
\sum_{k=1}^{n_0}\beta_k\mathsf{S}_k^\dagger=\mathbf{0}.
$$

The claim says that any implication among scaffold equations valid uniformly for association schemes is preserved by passage to the dual scaffolds; the source provides no resolution, so the statement remains open.
345116.disposition: Duality conjecture for planar scaffold equations: hypothesis and conclusion quantify over all association schemes with d>=delta classes; a refutation needs a universally valid implication plus a scheme where the dual fails; no bounded certificate. Parked.

345190.title: The unlabelled bridge-addable fragment-size conjecture
345190.statement_literal:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a class of graphs that is **bridge-addable**, meaning that adding an edge between vertices in distinct components preserves membership, and **decomposable**, meaning that a graph belongs to $\mathcal A$ if and only if each of its components does. For a graph $G$, define its **fragment size** by

$$
\operatorname{frag}(G)=|V(G)|-\max\{|V(C)|:C\text{ is a component of }G\}.
$$

Let $\tilde{R}_n \in_u\tilde{\mathcal A}$ be sampled uniformly from the unlabelled graphs in $\mathcal A$ on $n$ vertices. **Unlabelled bridge-addable fragment-size conjecture.** For each such graph class $\mathcal A$, there is a constant $c_{\mathcal A}$ such that, for each positive integer $n$,

$$
\mathbb E[\operatorname{frag}(\tilde{R}_n)]\leq c_{\mathcal A}.
$$

The labelled analogue has a uniform expectation bound, while the source gives an unlabelled example showing that the expectation can grow linearly for a particular class; the conjectured bound remains open in general.
345190.review_depth: full source TeX (McDiarmid arXiv:2001.05256 v2, 4 pages) read; web search for later work (none found)
345190.disposition: McDiarmid Conjecture 3 (bounded E[frag] for each bridge-addable decomposable class, unlabelled). Pairs with the parked 345188. The source's awkward example needs a different class for each k. Lane idea (not proved): a single class whose 2-edge-connected pieces are vertex-transitive (Cayley) graphs of super-sparse sizes k_i with per-vertex richness increasing level by level makes two-piece graphs dominate at n=2k_i, with P(disconnected) about 1/2, so E[frag] is about k_i/2 and unbounded. A rigorous proof needs counting isomorphism classes of Cayley graphs; asymptotic, no finite certificate, Lean-infeasible. Parked; recorded for root.

345617.title: Tree-factorization conjecture for mappings with small $(2,1)$-mapping content
345617.statement_literal:
Let $Q_0=[0,1]^3$ and let $f\colon Q_0\rightarrow X$ be a $1$-Lipschitz mapping into a metric space. Assume without loss of generality that $X\subseteq\ell_\infty$. A Lipschitz mapping **factors through a tree** if there are a tree $T$ and Lipschitz maps $g\colon Q_0\rightarrow T$ and $h\colon T\rightarrow X$ such that $f=h\circ g$. **Tree-factorization conjecture.**

If $\mathcal{H}^{2,1}_\infty(f,Q_0)=0$, then $f$ factors through a tree. Moreover, for every $\epsilon>0$, there is a $\delta=\delta(\epsilon)$ such that if $\mathcal{H}^{2,1}_\infty(f,Q_0)<\delta$, then there is a $1$-Lipschitz map $g\colon Q_0\rightarrow\ell_\infty$ that factors through a tree and satisfies

$$
\|g-f\|_\infty<\epsilon.
$$

This conjecture addresses the first unanswered case of the question of what can be said about a mapping when its $(2,1)$-mapping content is zero or small. Kaufman's construction and related examples show that no simple conclusion such as constancy is possible, while those examples factor through trees. The conjecture asks whether tree factorization characterizes the zero-content case and provides quantitative approximation in the small-content case.
345617.disposition: Tree-factorization conjecture for Lipschitz maps with small (2,1)-mapping content; quantitative metric geometry; parked.

345654.title: Burstein–Jones dominance conjecture for vincular-pattern statistics
345654.statement_literal:
Let $\mathfrak{D}^1_{2n}(\tau)$ be the Dumont-1 permutations of length $2n$ avoiding $\tau$. For a permutation $\pi$, let $(2\text{-}31)\pi$ and $(13\text{-}2)\pi$ be the numbers of occurrences of the indicated vincular patterns, where the dash indicates that the corresponding adjacent pattern letters need not be adjacent in $\pi$. Define

$$
a_{n,k}=|\{\pi\in\mathfrak{D}^1_{2n}(2143)\mid (2\text{-}31)\pi=k\}|,
$$

$$
b_{n,k}=|\{\pi\in\mathfrak{D}^1_{2n}(3421)\mid (13\text{-}2)\pi=k\}|.
$$

**Burstein–Jones's dominance conjecture.** For all $n\geq0$,

$$
a_{n,k}=b_{n,k}=1\quad\text{for }k=\binom{n}{2},\qquad a_{n,k}=b_{n,k}=0\quad\text{for }k>\binom{n}{2},
$$

and

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{m}a_{n,k}\geq\sum_{k=0}^{m}b_{n,k}\quad\text{for }0\leq m\leq\binom{n}{2},
$$

with equality when $m=\binom{n}{2}$. This refines the Wilf-equivalence conjecture by comparing distributions of vincular-pattern statistics; the source presents it as open and reports no proof beyond partial inroads.
345654.review_depth: full source TeX Section 5 (Burstein-Jones arXiv:2002.12189 v4 = DMTCS 2021) read incl. tables n=5,6,7; citing works arXiv:2610.01077 and arXiv:2610.30975 abstracts
345654.disposition: Burstein-Jones dominance Conjecture 5.3 (refinement of 2143~3421 on Dumont-1). The plain Wilf-equivalence was proved in Oct 2026 (Dong-Liu-Zhao arXiv:2610.01077; Zhang-Zhao arXiv:2610.30975, descent-top/ascent-top preserving bijections); neither abstract claims the (2-31)/(13-2) dominance. Exact enumerator (incremental 2143/3421 avoidance, vincular counts) cross-checked against brute force at n=4 and reproduces the source tables at n=7 exactly; extended to n=8 (168,503 permutations each side): dominance holds, tail slack 3,12,38,... n=9 exceeds the per-call cap (first entries 1,2 alone > 100 s). No counterexample; parked.

345968.title: Non-trivial automorphism conjecture for APN functions and permutations
345968.statement_literal:
Let $F\colon\mathbb{F}_2^n\rightarrow\mathbb{F}_2^n$ be an APN function, and let $\mathsf{Aut}(F)$ denote its automorphism group. If $F$ is an APN permutation, let $\mathsf{Aut_{LE}}(F)$ denote its group of LE-automorphisms. Two functions are **CCZ-equivalent** when their graphs are related by an affine permutation of the product space. **Non-trivial automorphism conjecture.** For every APN function $F\colon\mathbb{F}_2^n\rightarrow\mathbb{F}_2^n$, we have

$$
|\mathsf{Aut}(F)|>1.
$$

Moreover, if $F$ is an APN permutation, there exists a CCZ-equivalent permutation $G$ such that

$$
|\mathsf{Aut_{LE}}(G)|>1.
$$

All known APN functions have non-trivial automorphism groups, and all known APN permutations have a CCZ-equivalent representative with a non-trivial LE-automorphism; the conjecture asserts that these observed properties hold in general.
345968.disposition: Every APN function has a nontrivial automorphism (and APN permutations a CCZ-representative with nontrivial LE-automorphism). Quadratic APN functions always have translation automorphisms; a counterexample would be a new non-quadratic APN class; classification is complete only for n<=5. Parked (Lean Pool APN project concerns Kasami functions, unrelated).

346025.title: The local characterization conjecture for multiplier sets and cyclic direct factors
346025.statement_literal:
Let $m$, $n$, and $k$ be positive integers with $m\geq 2$, and suppose

$$
M=\{1,m,m^2,\ldots,m^{n-k-1},m^{i_0},m^{i_1},\ldots,m^{i_{k-1}}\},\qquad n\geq 2k+1.
$$

For a prime $p$ dividing $|G|$, write $\operatorname{ord}_p(m)$ for the multiplicative order of $m$ modulo $p$. Also let $\mathbb{Z}_{\omega}$ be a cyclic group of order $\omega$, and let $A=[0,n-k-1]\cup\{i_0,i_1,\ldots,i_{k-1}\}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{\omega}$ with $|A|=n$. **Local characterization conjecture.** The following assertions hold:

(i) $M$ splits an abelian group $G$ with $|M|=n$ if and only if, for every prime $p\mid |G|$,

$$
\{i_0,i_1,\ldots,i_{k-1}\}\equiv\{n-k,n-k+1,\ldots,n-1\}\pmod n
$$

and $n\mid\operatorname{ord}_p(m)$.

(ii) $A$ is a direct factor of $\mathbb{Z}_{\omega}$ if and only if

$$
\{i_0,i_1,\ldots,i_{k-1}\}\equiv\{n-k,n-k+1,\ldots,n-1\}\pmod n
$$

and $n\mid\omega$.

The source explains that part (i) and part (ii) are equivalent to the two preceding conjectures, respectively, and that they are known for $k\leq 2$; the general characterization remains open.
346025.review_depth: abstract (Zhao arXiv:2003.14006 v1); r161 record of sibling 346023 (parked after bounded search)
346025.disposition: Zhao local characterization conjecture for multiplier sets / cyclic direct factors; known for k<=2; same source family as the parked 346023 (r161 bounded search, no counterexample). Not repeated; parked.

346486.title: Ma–Ma–Yeh conjecture on partial gamma-positivity of generalized Stirling permutation polynomials
346486.statement_literal:
Let $n\geq 1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$. Write

$$
\Jsp_{n,i}(x,y,z):=\sum_{\pi\in\mathcal{JSP}_{n,i}}x^{\operatorname{asc}(\pi)}y^{\operatorname{des}(\pi)}z^{\operatorname{plat}(\pi)}
$$

for the trivariate extension of $A_{n,i}(y)$. A trivariate polynomial $p(x,y,z)=\sum_i s_i(x,y)z^i$ is **partial $\gamma$-positive** when every coefficient $s_i(x,y)$ is homogeneous $\gamma$-positive, meaning that it is homogeneous and can be written as

$$
s_i(x,y)=\sum_k\gamma_k(xy)^k(x+y)^{d-2k}
$$

with all $\gamma_k\geq 0$. **Ma–Ma–Yeh conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$, the polynomial $\Jsp_{n,i}(x,y,z)$ is partial $\gamma$-positive. The conjecture concerns the coefficientwise gamma-positivity of the ascent–descent–plateau enumerators for generalized Stirling permutations; its status is not resolved in the supplied source context.
346486.disposition: Ma-Ma-Yeh partial gamma-positivity conjecture for Jacobi-Stirling plateau/descent/ascent polynomials: the reserved source itself proves it ("Specialization ... confirms a recent partial gamma-positivity conjecture due to Ma, Yeh and the second named author").
